subject: Dedicated GPU capacity: architecture readout & scheduling
messages:
From: Ravi Gupta <ravi@finwave.com>

Cc: ops-eng@finwave.com
Date: Sun, 12 Jul 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated GPU capacity readout request (pool sizing / autoscale / isolation)

Hi Vivek / Marissa,

Thanks again for the quick demo last week. Our infra team (cc'd) would like a focused architecture readout on dedicated capacity: pool sizing, autoscaling behavior under noisy neighbors, and isolation/tenancy patterns. Specifically we want to validate predicted throughput vs our 99th/95th token-latency SLOs and discuss fallback options during burst periods.

Proposed format: 45–60 minute technical deep-dive with Q&A and a short runbook review. Can you run this next week? We are available Tue/Wed afternoon PT (Jul 20–21) or Thu (Jul 22) morning PT.

I've attached our current capacity workbook with baseline traffic and 90-day peaks. Please let us know what pre-reads you need.

Attachments: finwave_capacity_workbook.xlsx (spreadsheet)

Thanks,
Ravi
Ravi Gupta
Head of Infrastructure, FinWave
ravi@finwave.com

Date: Mon, 13 Jul 2026 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated GPU capacity readout request (pool sizing / autoscale / isolation)

Ravi — thanks for the workbook and the clear ask. We can do a technical readout and will prepare a short capacity model and a few failure/fallback scenarios.

Availability from our side this week is limited, but we can propose two slots:
- Fri Jul 23, 11:00–12:00 PT (recommended, 60 min)
- Mon Jul 26, 09:00–10:00 PT (alternate, 60 min)

Draft agenda attached: redwood_agenda_v1.pdf — short overview of serving/runtime constraints, pool sizing methodology (throughput vs concurrency), autoscale hysteresis and warm-cache strategies, isolation patterns (affinity, dedicated pools, cgroups/k8s-level isolation), and a 10-minute runbook/next-steps.

Pre-work requests: please populate the peak concurrency column in the workbook and call out any regions you want us to simulate. If you can share a short list of top request shapes (prompt lengths, streaming vs non-streaming) we can tailor perf numbers.

Marissa and Karthik will lead different sections: Marissa on autoscaling + fallback policy; Karthik on pool topology and kernel-selection tradeoffs. Kimberly will join for isolation and security controls.

I'll hold the Fri slot as tentative until you confirm.

—Vivek
Vivek Kulkarni
Head of Product (Capacity), Redwood Inference
